subject: Performance SLO qualification: context window, tokens, and latency impact
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Aliyah Hassan <aliyah.hassan@finco.com>, Ben Clarke <ben.clarke@finco.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Performance SLO qualification: context window, tokens, and latency impact

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and next steps from our discovery: 

- Goal: 99th percentile response latency <= 400ms for streaming assistant flows for customer support use case (multi-turn).
- Traffic shape: peak concurrency ~180 users, expected average throughput ~2.5 req/s, peak burst to 350 concurrent sessions possible during product launches.
- Prompt profile: average input payload ~6k tokens (mostly long conversation history), average model output ~150 tokens; some cases require full-document ingest up to ~20k tokens as a single prompt.
- Streaming: client expects token-level streaming with first-byte latency < 200ms and steady streaming thereafter.

Attached: SLO_requirements.xlsx and high-level perf matrix (redwood-performance-matrix.pdf).

Questions we raised for qualification: 
1) How often will you send full-document 20k token requests vs. incremental conversation updates? (helps with batching/kv cache planning)
2) Are you able to truncate history or send summarized context in some flows to reduce context window?
3) Any hard constraints on concurrency per session (long-lived connections) vs bursty stateless requests?

Next steps:
- Could you send the distribution of input sizes (CSV is fine) and a short list of 10 representative prompts we can use for perf testing?
- We'll schedule a 60-minute technical perf call with our runtime engineers to walk through streaming and tokenization impacts (proposed Wed 7/1 10am PT).

If that works, I'll loop in Vivek (CS lead) and Rishi (AE) to coordinate the test plan.

Best,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Aliyah Hassan <aliyah.hassan@finco.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Clarke <ben.clarke@finco.com>
Date: Wed, 01 Jul 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance SLO qualification: context window, tokens, and latency impact

Thanks Marissa, great recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Distribution: ~70% of requests are conversation updates (avg 4k tokens including history), ~25% are mid-sized docs (10-12k tokens), ~5% are full-doc ingestion (18-22k tokens). I'll attach anonymized CSV by EOD.
- Streaming: we need per-token streaming for the chat UI. First-byte latency under 250ms is acceptable, but <200ms would be ideal.
- Concurrency: each user holds a websocket connection; typical per-connection request rate is low (0.02 req/s) but high concurrency as noted.

One ask: can you confirm whether Redwood's current runtime supports KV cache reuse across sessions for conversation history to avoid resending full context? Also curious how model choice (e.g., 32k vs 64k context model or quantized variants) affects latency.

We'll join the tech call tomorrow.

Aliyah Hassan
Head of Product, FinCo

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Aliyah Hassan <aliyah.hassan@finco.com>, Ben Clarke <ben.clarke@finco.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 01 Jul 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance SLO qualification: context window, tokens, and latency impact

Aliyah, thanks for the details, that distribution is super helpful. Quick answers and what we'll bring to the technical call: 

- KV cache: Redwood supports prefix/KV cache reuse for session-affine interactions. For websocket flows we keep an active KV cache keyed by session id which avoids re-sending full tokenizer tokens when the model supports incremental KV usage. That will significantly reduce end-to-end input size for repeated turns (depends on retention policy and TTL you want).

- Model/context choices: 32k-context models generally have lower end-to-end latency than 64k models for the same compute class, but larger context capacity reduces the need to repeatedly fetch or summarize history. Quantized variants (INT8/INT4) lower compute latency and memory footprint but can slightly increase CPU overhead for dequant ops; in practice we often see 10-20% cost/perf improvement with negligible quality regression for many workloads. We'll bring measured examples.

- Streaming first-byte latency: Achievable with our streaming runtime when running on dedicated instances and with optimized kernel selection; the main factors are model size, context length of the request, and network RTT. For your distribution, we'll produce a table showing expected P50/P90/P99 latencies across the three request size buckets using both 32k and 64k variants.

Attached a short perf matrix and example test plan. For tomorrow's call we'll ask for a representative set of 10 prompts plus the CSV of sizes. Also would like to capture your failure mode: is it preferable to return a partial streamed response under high load or to queue/reject?

Forwarding meeting invite to schedule the deep-dive.

Best,
Marissa
[Attachment: redwood-performance-matrix.pdf]

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 02 Jul 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Performance SLO qualification: context window, tokens, and latency impact

Marissa / Vivek, quick internal note prior to the call: 

- Commercial implication: if FinCo truly needs sustained 350 concurrent websocket sessions with 20k token documents, Dedicated capacity with pinned GPUs looks like the safest path to meet 99th percentile SLAs. Hosted shared pool might struggle during correlated bursts.
- Pricing: we should prepare a reserved capacity option (monthly commit) and a burst tier for occasional spikes. Also include a pilot price for the perf testing window.
- Engineering ask for the call: confirm whether we can demo KV cache TTL behavior and show a before/after latency delta for a 6k->20k historical window.

I'll join the technical demo and handle pricing discussion.

Rishi

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Aliyah Hassan <aliyah.hassan@finco.com>, Ben Clarke <ben.clarke@finco.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 02 Jul 2026 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance SLO qualification: context window, tokens, and latency impact

Thanks everyone — short summary and confirmed next steps from the tech call we just scheduled: 

1) FinCo to send: anonymized CSV of request-size distribution + 10 representative prompts (Aliyah) — due EOD 7/2.
2) Redwood to deliver: perf matrix for P50/P90/P99 for three buckets (4k, 10-12k, 18-22k) across 32k and 64k model variants; KV cache demo showing latency reduction for multi-turn sessions; recommended Dedicated capacity sizing and pilot pricing (Rishi) — deliverable by 7/7.
3) Test window: propose 48-hour pilot run with sample traffic (we'll provide instructions and a shared network endpoint). We'll include an attachment with the network diagram and test checklist.
4) Failure mode: default behavior will be graceful degradation — partial streamed response + explicit status code when model truncation occurs. We'll surface this on the API and provide a fall-back policy to a smaller model variant if latency exceeds target.

Please confirm if any of the above items need adjustment. Thanks again — looking forward to the perf test.

Regards,
Marissa
